title: Fire Wall, Fire Barrier or Fire Partition? How to Tell Which One You're Drawing
summary: Fire wall vs fire barrier vs fire partition: what each separates under the IBC, typical ratings, how far each runs, and how to keep rated walls right in Revit.
body_markdown:
FAQ


## Frequently asked questions.


Can't find what you're looking for?
Get in touch .


### What is a fire barrier?


A fire barrier is a fire-resistance-rated wall that separates parts of one building, such as exit stairways, shafts, fire areas and separated occupancies. It runs from the floor or foundation below to the deck above, and its rating comes from the section of the code that requires it.


### What is the difference between a fire wall and a fire barrier?


A fire wall divides a structure into separate buildings, runs from the foundation through the roof and must stay standing if either side collapses. A fire barrier separates spaces within one building, runs floor to deck, and has no collapse requirement.


### What is the difference between a fire barrier and a fire partition?


A fire barrier encloses exit stairs, shafts and occupancy separations, carries the rating set by the code section that requires it and must reach the deck above. A fire partition protects corridors and dwelling or sleeping units, is usually rated 1 hour, and may stop at a rated ceiling.


### What is a fire barrier called in the UK?


The closest UK terms are a compartment wall or compartment floor, which divide a building into fire compartments under Approved Document B. Cavity barriers do a related job inside concealed spaces.


### What is a fire-rated wall?


A fire-rated wall is a wall assembly tested to resist fire for a set time, usually 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours. Fire walls, fire barriers and fire partitions are all fire-rated walls, with different rules for where they're required and how far they run.


### Does a fire partition have to go to the deck?


Not always. A fire partition can stop at a ceiling assembly rated at least as long as the partition, and corridor walls can stop at a qualifying corridor ceiling. Otherwise it runs from the floor below to the underside of the deck above.
